about: Verbatim excerpts from every source this guide cites, saved so each fact can be traced and re-checked. Excerpts are short; see each URL (and its archived copy, when added) for full context.

sources.publisher: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore
sources.title: Tourism to Cape Cod National Seashore contributes $754 million to local economy (Sept. 26, 2025)

excerpts.quote: A new National Park Service report shows that 3.8 million visitors to Cape Cod National Seashore in 2024 spent $598 million in communities near the park.
When Congress set aside 44,000 acres in 1961, it was the first time a national park was carved out of such a populated area.
excerpts.supports: 44,000 acres in 1961; first national park carved out of such a populated area

excerpts.quote: An experiment in cooperative stewardship, it was an attempt to conserve a treasured resource in partnership with six towns and some 600 private landowners within its boundaries.
excerpts.supports: cooperative stewardship with six towns and some 600 private landowners

excerpts.quote: The national seashore occupies much of outer Cape Cod, a large peninsula extending 60 miles into the Atlantic from the coast of Massachusetts.
excerpts.supports: peninsula extending 60 miles; seashore occupies much of the outer Cape

excerpts.quote: Cape Cod National Seashore is on the Atlantic Flyway
More than 40 species rest and feed on the beaches, including federally endangered roseate terns.
excerpts.supports: more than 40 bird species; roseate terns

sources.publisher: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore
sources.title: Cape Cod National Seashore (home page)

excerpts.quote: Forty miles of pristine sandy beach, marshes, ponds, and uplands support diverse species. Lighthouses, cultural landscapes, and wild cranberry bogs offer a glimpse of Cape Cod's past
excerpts.supports: forty miles of beach, marshes, ponds, uplands; lighthouses, cultural landscapes, cranberry bogs

excerpts.quote: Choose from one of eleven hiking trails at Cape Cod National Seashore.
Enjoy Six National Seashore Beaches Swim when there are lifeguards on duty, from late June through Labor Day.
excerpts.supports: six beaches; lifeguards late June through Labor Day

sources.publisher: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore
sources.title: Operating Hours & Seasons

excerpts.quote: Cape Cod National Seashore is open year-round. The most popular months to visit the park are June through September.
excerpts.supports: open year-round; most popular months June–September

excerpts.quote: During the busy summer season, all roads and facilities are open and a full range of programs are available to enjoy. From November through April, some visitor facilities are closed.
excerpts.supports: summer: all roads and facilities open; Nov–Apr some facilities closed

excerpts.quote: Lifeguards are typically on duty at the six national seashore beaches from late June through Labor Day.
Restrooms at Salt Pond Visitor Center in Eastham and Province Lands Visitor Center in Provincetown are open year-round. Other restrooms in the park are open seasonally from late spring to early fall.

sources.publisher: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore
sources.title: Visitor Centers

excerpts.quote: Salt Pond Visitor Center is Cape Cod National Seashore's year-round visitor orientation facility. Located in Eastham
The Province Lands Visitor Center is open from May through October.

sources.publisher: National Park Service, Cape Cod National Seashore
sources.title: Fees & Passes

excerpts.quote: This park does not accept cash. ... Private Vehicle $25.00 Pass is for one private, non-commercial vehicle
Per Person $15.00 Pass is for one person 16 years of age or older — entering on foot or by bicycle.
excerpts.supports: $15 per person, 16 and older, foot or bike

excerpts.quote: Annual Entrance - Park $60.00 Passes are available at beach entrances during times when fees are normally collected. ... Valid for the current season.
The pass permits access to any of the six Cape Cod National Seashore beaches late-May through mid-September during that calendar year.

Entrance fees are only required seasonally at park beaches and are not required in most other parts of the park. Cape Cod National Seashore beach entrance fees are collected in spring, summer, and fall.
excerpts.supports: fees seasonal, beaches only; collected spring/summer/fall

excerpts.quote: All passes (including the America the Beautiful series) are only sold during the months that the fees are collected. Passes can ONLY be purchased at beach entrances and are NOT sold at park visitor centers.
excerpts.supports: passes only at beach entrances, only in fee months

sources.title: Cape Cod Bridges Program Final Environmental Impact Statement, Chapter 1: Introduction

excerpts.quote: These bridges — which provide the only roadway connections between Cape Cod and the mainland
the Cape Cod peninsula in Barnstable County, which comprises 15 towns with a year-round population of approximately 230,000 residents.
These bridges also serve as the gateway to Cape Cod for millions of annual visitors to the region during the height of the popular summer tourist season between Memorial Day and Labor Day.
excerpts.supports: millions of annual visitors; Memorial Day–Labor Day

sources.title: Cape Cod Bridges Program FEIS, Chapter 4, Section 4.4: Maritime Transportation, Traffic, and Safety

excerpts.quote: Cape Cod Canal is a sea-level 17.4-mile-long navigable waterway
an 8.1-mile-long land cut connecting Buzzards Bay in the southwest and Cape Cod Bay in the northeast.
excerpts.supports: land cut connecting Buzzards Bay and Cape Cod Bay

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Department of Transportation (sourced from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers)
sources.title: History of the Cape Cod Canal and bridges

excerpts.quote: Finally, on July 29, 1914, the Cape Cod Canal was opened as a privately operated toll waterway
the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) assumed control over the canal in 1928.
The bridges were built simultaneously, and were dedicated on June 22, 1935, and then opened to traffic.
excerpts.supports: bridges dedicated June 22, 1935, then opened to traffic

sources.title: Cape Cod Canal Transportation Study, Chapter 2: Existing Environmental Conditions

excerpts.quote: The study team collected traffic data during a summer period and a non summer period in 2014
daily traffic volumes on the Bourne and Sagamore Bridge are 49% and 59% higher in the summer, respectively, compared to non-summer periods.
the average traffic volumes crossing the Canal Bridges during February are only 54% (Bourne Bridge) to 60% (Sagamore Bridge) of the volumes crossing these bridges during August.
summer Saturday peak period, a period of high traffic demand because vacation rentals on the Cape generally begin and end on Saturday.
